page: Amazon Web Services c9g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit ARM architecture. The server features 96 dedicated physical cores based on the AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor operating at 3.3 GHz, with a single thread per core. The processor is configured with 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 96 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 192.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage and contains zero dedicated GPUs. Network performance is anchored by a 50 Gbps baseline interface.

Benchmark results show exceptional multi-threaded execution and memory bandwidth. The instance achieved top-tier performance in multi-core stress-ng tests (192,014.4) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (1,131.71 GB/sec), driven by the dedicated 96-core count without simultaneous multithreading contention. Memory throughput is equally robust, reaching 13,912.96 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 363.83 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads. In operational database benchmarks, the server handled 269.45 million Redis SET operations per second and demonstrated 198.56 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU inference for medium language models registered strong performance at 234.67 prompt tokens per second.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio delivers high compute density for parallel computational jobs without paying for unneeded memory capacity. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage requires external network storage integration, such as Amazon EBS, for persistent or high-throughput local disk operations. The instance is well matched for compute-bound batch processing, high-volume web serving, Redis caching layers, microservices clusters, and distributed continuous integration and deployment pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by 96 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 cores running at 3.3 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. Featuring 192.0 GB of system memory, the instance maintains a balanced 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio tailored for CPU-intensive workloads. It does not bundle local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-core compute capability, high uncached memory bandwidth of 363.83 GB/sec, and strong key-value throughput with over 269 million Redis SET operations per second. The server offers dense multi-threaded compute efficiency, though applications needing fast disk access require external storage attachments. This profile fits high-throughput web serving, parallel batch computation, media transcoding, and distributed build pipelines.
